THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 28/07/2018, PASSED IN MVC NO.11/2014, ON THE FILE OF THE II ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES,
HASSAN, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.2,97,728/- WITH INTEREST 8% FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS REALIZATION.
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The insurer as well as claimant is in appeal.

2. The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,97,728/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
3. The Tribunal has held that the insurer would be liable to pay the compensation.

The insurer,
however, in his appeal contended that the involvement of the vehicle itself was not established and that the owner of the vehicle did not possess the requisite licence.
4. The claimant, on the other hand, contends that the sums awarded is inadequate inasmuch as the income taken by itself was improper.

5. The evidence on record indicates that FIR was registered against the driver of the autorickshaw in which the claimants were travelling and subsequently a chargesheet was also laid against the driver of the autorickshaw.
These facts thus establish the occurance of the accident.

It is also to be stated here that the damages are indicated in the IMV report and the wound certificate issued to the claimant indicated the injuries suffered and in the records, it has been recorded that the injuries were as a result of a road traffic accident and these facts confirm the fact that an accident did occur as a result of the use of the autorikshaw.

sentences.text: In the light of this evidence, the contention of the insurer that the vehicle therein was not involved in the accident
cannot be accepted.
7. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.

In my view, having regard to the avocation of the claimant and the nature of injury, it would have a direct bearing on the earning capacity, hence it would be appropriate to determine the disability at 10% to the whole body.
8. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.5,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2013, would be Rs.8,000/-.
9. As the claimant was aged 35 years, a multiplier of '16' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,53,600/- (Rs.8,000/- x 12 x '16' x 10%) towards 'loss of future income' .
10. As a consequence, the amount of Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.24,000/- (Rs.8,000/- X 3 months).
11. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.40,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

13. The sums awarded under the heads 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges',
'medical expenses' and 'future medical expenses' are just and proper and hence confirmed.

14. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
 Sl. Particulars Award by Award by  No. Tribunal this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 50,000/- 60,000/-

2 . Medical expenses 65,928/- 65,928/-
 3. conveyance, food and 25,000/- 25,000/-
 nourishment and  attendant charges  4. Loss of income during 15,000/- 24,000/-
 laid up period  5. Loss of future income 76,800/- 1,53,600/-
 6. Loss of amenities in 40,000/- 50,000/-
 life

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.4,03,528/- as against Rs.2,97,728/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

17. On such deposit, Rs.3,00,000/- is ordered to be invested in the name of claimant for a period of five years in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of his choice renewable for another period of three years with liberty to withdraw the interest accrued thereon periodically.
After maturity, the Bank shall release the amount in favour of claimant without any further proceedings.
The remaining amount shall be released in favour of claimant through account payee cheque after proper identification.
18. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
. The appeal filed by insurer is dismissed and the appeal filed by claimant is accordingly allowed in part.
